input.quote: then such Dispute shall be submitted to the International Centre for Dispute Resolution ("ICDR") for final and binding arbitration pursuant to the arbitration clause set forth in Section 15.10.2.
input.rationale: Section 15.9 (p0822) picks Delaware internal law, which sits at our accepted fallback for governing law. However, Section 15.10 (p0823-p0824) does not give us the corresponding Delaware courts: all unresolved Disputes must go to final and binding ICDR international arbitration under its International Arbitration Rules (p0826-p0827), with only IP-ownership matters carved out to "a U.S. federal court of appropriate jurisdiction" and a customary preliminary-injunction carve-out. That fails the fallback forum element on a material term (arbitration is not the corresponding Delaware or California courts), although it is not walk-away territory because the seat is New York rather than abroad. We therefore redlined at the fallback level only: unresolved Disputes (including IP-ownership matters, whose retained arbitration cross-reference would otherwise dangle) go exclusively to the Delaware state and federal courts, and Section 15.10.2 is conformed so the ICDR process operates only where the Parties later agree in writing to arbitrate. We left the narrow Section 7.5.5 AAA expert determination on Material Impact (p0553) and the preliminary injunctive relief carve-out untouched as pre-existing, narrow mechanics.

ops.oldText: then such Dispute shall be submitted to the International Centre for Dispute Resolution ("ICDR") for final and binding arbitration pursuant to the arbitration clause set forth in Section 15.10.2. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no matters relating to breach or alleged breach of the ownership of intellectual property or rights in intellectual property or the validity or enforceability thereof shall be resolved by arbitration, but rather shall be determined by a U.S. federal court of appropriate jurisdiction.
ops.newText: then such Dispute, including any matter relating to breach or alleged breach of the ownership of intellectual property or rights in intellectual property or the validity or enforceability thereof, shall be brought exclusively in the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware, and each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts.

ops.oldText: Either Party shall have the right to initiate arbitration at any time after the expiration of thirty (30) days after a Dispute is notified to the Executive Officers.
ops.newText: Either Party shall have the right to initiate arbitration of a Dispute only if the Parties mutually agree in writing to submit that Dispute to arbitration.

ops.oldText: Any Dispute including the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be determined by the ICDR
ops.newText: Any Dispute so submitted to arbitration by mutual written agreement, including the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be determined by the ICDR

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Delaware governing law is acceptable to us, but we cannot accept mandatory ICDR international arbitration as the merits forum; we have sent unresolved Disputes (including intellectual property ownership matters) to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts that correspond to the chosen law, and conformed Section 15.10.2 so arbitration applies only where the Parties later agree in writing. The existing right to seek preliminary injunctive relief in any court is preserved.
proposal.summary: Unresolved Disputes go to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts; the ICDR arbitration process applies only if the Parties later agree in writing to arbitrate.
